items.prompt: Black to move on move five. Three of these four replies are within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16). Which one is not?

claims.statement: ...c5, ...h6 and ...Bf5 are each within 40 cp of the top move (depth 16).
...Be6 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move.
The knight on g5 attacks e6.

hints: Which of the four squares for Black's pieces does the knight on g5 attack?
The knight attacks e6, so a bishop there can be taken.
items.explain: The knight on g5 attacks e6, so a bishop placed there can be traded off at once and Black's pawn structure is broken by the recapture. The other three moves do not walk into the knight's range. Engine, depth 16: ...Be6 is at least 150 centipawns behind the best move; the other three are within 40.

items.prompt: Black has answered with ...c5. Does 6.Nxf7 score at least 150 centipawns worse than the engine's best move (depth 16)?

claims.statement: Taking on f7 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Count the material first: a knight for a pawn.
The king can take the knight, so the fork gains nothing.
Yes.
items.explain: After ...c5 nothing defends the knight on f7 and the king can take it, so White has given a knight for a pawn. The engine at depth 16 rates the sacrifice at least 150 centipawns worse than the best move.

items.prompt: Black has declined with ...Bf5. White to move: find a quiet move that develops a piece or supports d4 and is within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16). Edge-pawn moves such as a3 or h3 also score close, but this item accepts only developing moves and the c-pawn move.

claims.statement: Ne2, Bd3, N5f3, c3 and Bc4 are each within 40 cp of the top move (depth 16).
Taking on f7 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move.

hints: The bishop on f5 attacks the c2 pawn and the e4 square.
White wants a safe developing move, not a sacrifice.
Ne2, Bd3, N5f3, c3 or Bc4.
items.explain: The bishop on f5 looks at the queenside and the centre, and the sacrifice on f7 no longer has the h6 pawn pushing the knight. Quiet development with Ne2, Bd3, Bc4 or the retreat to f3, or c3 to support d4, keeps all the material. Engine, depth 16: those five are within 40 centipawns of the top move; taking on f7 is at least 150 behind.

feedback_by_move.g5f7: The king takes the knight and White has only given up material.

items.prompt: Black to move on move five. Three of these four replies are within 40 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16); one is at least 100 centipawns worse. Which one is worse?

claims.statement: ...c5, ...h6 and ...Bf5 are each within 40 cp of the top move (depth 16).
...e5 is at least 100 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Look at which diagonals each reply opens or closes.
One reply opens a line towards f7, which the knight already attacks.
items.explain: ...h6, ...c5 and ...Bf5 keep Black's pieces safe and fight for the centre. ...e5 opens the diagonal from f1 to f7, so Bc4 adds a second attacker on a pawn that only the king defends. Engine, depth 16: the first three are within 40 centipawns of the top move; ...e5 is at least 100 behind.

items.prompt: Black has played the king to d7. White to move: find the move within 80 centipawns of the engine's top move (depth 16).

claims.statement: Nxf7 and Bc4 are each within 80 cp of the top move (depth 16).
After Nxf7 White is ahead by at least 5 pawns (depth 16).

hints: The knight has a square that attacks two black units.
Can any black piece take a knight on f7?
Nxf7 (Bc4 also keeps a big edge).
items.explain: The knight takes on f7 and attacks the queen on d8 and the rook on h8. The king on d7 is not next to f7, and no other black piece attacks the square, so Black cannot take the knight. One of the two attacked pieces will be lost. Engine, depth 16: Nxf7 is the top move and White is ahead by more than five pawns; the quiet Bc4 is also within 80 centipawns.

claims.statement: Be2, N5f3, Ne2, f3 and Qd2 are each within 40 cp of the top move (depth 16).

hints: What does the bishop on g4 attack?
Something on the d1-g4 diagonal is attacked. Block the diagonal or move the piece.
Be2, N5f3, Ne2, f3 or Qd2 all deal with it.
items.explain: The bishop on g4 attacks the queen along the diagonal g4-d1. Putting a piece or pawn on e2 or f3 blocks it, and moving the queen away also works. The sacrifice on f7 does not help. Engine, depth 16: those five are within 40 centipawns of the top move; taking on f7 is at least 150 behind.

items.explain: After the capture no white piece attacks f7, so the knight is undefended and the king takes it. White has given a knight for a pawn.

items.prompt: Compare with the position where White's bishop is still on f1. Here White's bishop stands on c4 instead. White plays the knight to f7. Can Black's king take it?

items.explain: The bishop on c4 looks along the open diagonal at f7, so the knight is defended and the king may not capture it. The fork on the queen and rook now wins material.
